en: The Therāpadāna:
The Chapter on the Giver of a Support (Ālambaṇadāyakavagga) 10.
The Apadāna of the Elder Ekavandanīya (He Who Is to Be Worshipped Alone)
With a clear mind and joyful heart, [I praise] Vessabhu, the bull-like, excellent, heroic, and victorious one.
I paid homage to the Best of Buddhas.
That deed which I performed back then, thirty-one eons ago—
I do not recall being born in an evil state;
this is the fruit of my salutation.
Within twenty-four eons—
Named Vikatānanda,
he was a wheel-turning monarch of great power, endowed with the seven treasures.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Ekavaṇḍaniya spoke these verses.
The legend of the elder Ekavaṇḍaniya is the tenth.
The twenty-third chapter, the Ālambanadāyaka-vagga, is concluded.
Its summary verse:
The object, the antelope skin,
and the one who gave the flesh, the wood, and the thorn.
Abyādhi, Aṅkola, Soṇṇa, Miñja,
Āveḷa, and Vandana—
these fifty-five verses.
They have been reckoned by those who see the goal.
